description: A single grouped bar chart (no sub-panels) plotting Microhardness (HV) on the y-axis, scaled 0-700 with numerically labelled ticks every 100, against three categorical samples on the x-axis, printed as "Sample 1", "Sample 2" and "Sample 3" — the three Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si alloy compositions of the study. A two-entry legend distinguishes light-blue bars ("Predicted values") from pink bars ("Experimental values"); each blue predicted bar carries a black vertical error bar. Printed data labels give, for Sample 1: predicted 521 HV vs experimental 515 HV with error 1.17 %; for Sample 2: predicted 490 HV vs experimental 500 HV with error 2.00 %; for Sample 3: predicted 415 HV vs experimental 424 HV with error 2.09 %. Bar heights therefore decrease monotonically from Sample 1 to Sample 3, and the largest printed value is 521 HV (predicted, Sample 1). Predicted exceeds experimental in Samples 1 and 3 but falls slightly below it in Sample 2. The figure demonstrates that the machine-learning model reproduces measured microhardness of these alloys within about 2 %, i.e. the predicted and experimental bar pairs are nearly coincident, with error bars overlapping in every sample.

subfigures.description: Grouped bar chart with paired bars per category: blue = Predicted values, pink = Experimental values, for Sample 1, Sample 2 and Sample 3. y-axis 'Microhardness (HV)', 0-700 in steps of 100. Printed pairs/errors: 521 vs 515 (1.17 %), 490 vs 500 (2.00 %), 415 vs 424 (2.09 %); black error bars on the predicted bars.

observations.observation: The figure is a single grouped bar chart with two bars per sample category, coloured light blue and pink, explained by a legend reading 'Predicted values' and 'Experimental values'.
The y-axis is labelled 'Microhardness (HV)' and is scaled from 0 to 700 with labelled ticks at 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600 and 700.
The x-axis carries three categories printed exactly as 'Sample 1', 'Sample 2' and 'Sample 3'.
For Sample 1 the printed values are predicted 521 HV and experimental 515 HV, with the printed error '1.17%'.
For Sample 2 the printed values are predicted 490 HV and experimental 500 HV, with the printed error '2.00%'.
For Sample 3 the printed values are predicted 415 HV and experimental 424 HV, with the printed error '2.09%'.
Black vertical error bars are drawn on the bars; their magnitudes are not numerically labelled, but in every sample the predicted and experimental error-bar spans visibly overlap.
The measured microhardness decreases monotonically across the three samples, from the Sample 1 pair (521/515 HV) down to the Sample 3 pair (415/424 HV).
The caption states the figure shows predicted versus actual microhardness of three samples of Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si alloys.

The citing text states the minimum error between predicted and experimental value was 1.17 %, lower than 2.01 % and 2.96 % reported for hardness prediction of high entropy alloys by Ren et al. [14] and Huang et al. [47].

The citing text states the microhardness of the samples can reach 515 HV and attributes this to solid solution phases; note the figure prints a higher value of 521 HV for the predicted Sample 1 bar, while 515 HV is the highest experimental value shown.

The citing text reports the samples' δ values span 0.0335 to 0.0595 (below 0.066) and ΔH_mix spans −1.213 to −0.451 kJ/mol, falling inside the −11.6 to 3.2 kJ/mol solid-solution window; none of these parameters are plotted in the figure.

unreadable_items: error-bar magnitudes are drawn but not numerically labelled, so the standard deviations cannot be read
